questions.question: If a package contains liquid containers, the box must display:

options.text: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
The number of containers inside the box.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Packages with liquid containers must show arrows. The arrows must point in the correct upright direction.

questions.question: Which type of material may need a transport index?
questions.correctAnswerText: Radioactive
questions.explanation: Radioactive materials may need a transport index. This number shows how much control is needed during transport. All cargo in one vehicle cannot have a total transport index higher than 50.

questions.question: Hazardous materials shipping papers may not be kept:

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's door.
In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
Within reach of the driver while the seat belt is fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be easy to reach in an emergency. Keep papers in a pouch on the driver's door or in clear view within reach while your seat belt is on. You can keep papers on the driver's seat when you are not in the vehicle.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials containers, do not use:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hooks.
questions.explanation: Protect hazardous materials containers. Never use equipment that could damage containers, such as hooks.

questions.question: A material's hazard class shows:

options.text: The risks associated with the material.
How quickly the material must reach its destination.

questions.correctAnswerText: The risks associated with the material.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are placed into one of nine classes. Each class explains the type of risks the material has.

questions.question: If you find that your cargo is leaking, you should:

options.text: Touch the leaking material to identify the cargo.
Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
Assume all the cargo is leaking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
questions.explanation: If you find a leak in hazardous materials cargo, use the shipping papers, labels, or package location to identify what is leaking. Do not touch the leaking material.

questions.question: How do you label a package if the hazardous materials label will not fit on the package?

options.text: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the item.
Attach a QR Code to be scanned.
Reduce the size of the HazMat label to fit it completely on the item.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the item.
questions.explanation: Place diamond-shaped hazard warning labels on hazardous materials packages. If the label will not fit on the package, place it on a tag that is securely attached to the package.

questions.question: ____ are used to warn others of hazardous materials.
questions.correctAnswerText: Placards
questions.explanation: Placards are diamond-shaped signs placed on bulk packages and vehicles to warn others of hazardous materials. The shipper must place the placards. The driver must verify that the correct placards are in place.

questions.question: As a driver, which of the following is not your job at an accident scene?

options.text: Keeping people away from the scene.
Trying to put the fire out yourself.
Telling emergency personnel about the hazardous materials danger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trying to put the fire out yourself.
questions.explanation: At an accident scene with hazardous materials, your job is to keep people away, limit spilled material if safe, and inform emergency personnel of the dangers. Do not fight hazardous materials fires unless you have protective equipment and training.

questions.question: If transporting hazardous materials, warn others by:

options.text: Posting HazMat placards on your truck.
Putting flashing lights on your truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Posting HazMat placards on your truck.
questions.explanation: Shippers of hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs called placards on vehicles. Shippers must provide placards, labels, shipping papers, and emergency response information.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees receive training and testing?
questions.correctAnswerText: Once every three years
questions.explanation: All drivers must receive training on hazardous materials transportation security. This training covers how to recognize and respond to security threats. Employees must receive training and testing at least once every three years.

questions.question: Why can opening trailer doors during a cargo fire make the fire worse?

options.text: It allows oxygen into the trailer.
It changes the temperature of the trailer.
It provides more moisture to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows oxygen into the trailer.
questions.explanation: During a cargo fire, opening the trailer doors is dangerous. Oxygen enters the area and can cause the fire to flare up and spread.

questions.question: Where should a hazardous material's identification number appear?

options.text: On a sticker near the shipping container.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the material's packaging.
questions.explanation: The ID number must appear on the shipping paper and on the packaging. It also must appear on cargo tanks and other bulk packaging.

questions.question: If your planned route has restrictions, who should you contact?
questions.correctAnswerText: The California Highway Patrol
questions.explanation: Contact the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and/or the California Highway Patrol (CHP) for information about permits and route restrictions for hazardous materials.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials warning placards?
questions.correctAnswerText: A diamond
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: When loading corrosive materials, what should you NOT do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Roll the containers
questions.explanation: When loading by hand, load breakable containers of corrosive liquid one at a time. Keep them upright. Do not drop or roll the containers.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, how far must you park from the nearest building?
questions.correctAnswerText: 300 feet
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. You can park closer only for short periods when necessary, such as refueling.

questions.question: While driving, where should shipping papers be kept?
questions.correctAnswerText: Within reach
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be kept where you can easily reach them while wearing your seat belt. Keep them in a pouch in the driver's side door or another easily accessible location. They must be clearly visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: How should a placard be placed on a vehicle?

options.text: At least three inches away from any other markings
Under a ladder if space is limited
On a background that matches the placard color

questions.correctAnswerText: At least three inches away from any other markings
questions.explanation: A placard must be at least three inches away from any other markings. Keep it clear of attachments like doors and ladders. Always place the placard against a background of a contrasting color.

questions.question: What do you need to know to choose the correct placard?

options.text: The hazard class of the materials
The type of container holding the materials

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard class of the materials
questions.explanation: To choose the correct placard, you must know the hazard class of the materials, the amount being shipped, and the total weight of all hazardous materials in your vehicle.
